basics.name: Stéphan Mestach
basics.label: Senior developer
basics.summary: Don't make the same mistake twice. 25 years of software, from Java insurance applications to data systems for public health. I like spotting problems before they hit production, explaining them clearly, and turning each fix into a tool, a test or a runbook so it stays fixed. Pragmatic, moving things forward without analysis paralysis, available when someone is stuck. Believe in modular code, good APIs, automated tests, continuous integration, monitoring and open source.

work.name: Bluesquare
work.summary: Nine years on data systems for public health programs. Started around DHIS2, the open-source health information system used by many ministries of health to collect and analyse their data: performance-based financing on top of it (ORBF2 / Hesabu), then running and troubleshooting around 50 DHIS2 servers. Then beyond DHIS2: IASO, Bluesquare's georegistry and data collection platform (its DHIS2 integration and performance), and lately data pipelines and lightweight apps for health campaigns on OpenHEXA, Bluesquare's data platform. Common thread: keeping these systems working as projects scale and data comes in.
highlights: Performance-based financing: ORBF2 / Hesabu rule engine (think Excel on top of your DHIS2), rolled out in Liberia, DRC, Cameroon, Ethiopia, ...
From data collection to DHIS2: ONA forms first, then IASO form mappings, org unit sync and compatibility across DHIS2 versions
Running DHIS2 in production: around 50 instances, diagnose report, runbooks, automated reviews, on-premise local hosting

Scaling with the projects: larger org unit pyramids, more entities and submissions, faster exports and mobile sync, bottlenecks found with dedicated tooling (explain_request, QueryProfiler, APM from access logs)
Watching the data coming in: monitoring submissions and imports, detecting inconsistencies, correcting at the source (configuration changes, production data fixes through scripts)
Data with DuckDB and Parquet: IASO exports, OpenHEXA campaign pipelines, "pre-baked apps" served from Parquet and PMTiles
DHIS2 community: helping other implementers and reporting issues to the DHIS2 core team (~270 posts, 14 accepted solutions since 2019)

work.name: Credoc
work.summary: Coaching junior developers, preparing sprints and estimations with analysts and project managers, technical design with the solution architect (java, spring, jersey 2, spring-batch, spring-boot, hystrix, sql-server, raml).
highlights: Introduced a build and deployment pipeline (maven, bamboo, sonar, liquibase, smoke tests, soap-ui acceptance tests, gatling load tests) and a code review workflow
Address Service: merged the national and 3 regional data sources (millions of records) with spring batch, REST API for address completion and translation to NIS codes
Person Service: Fedict person services exposed as a human readable REST model, with circuit breakers (hystrix)
Training box: mock and standalone versions of the applications for offline / poor connectivity training
Demand Forms: forms filled by notaries for deed events targeting banks and the Walloon administration; design, task split, phasing, estimations, code reviews
Architecture improvements: user and contribution guides, mutation testing, tooling to display dependencies between applications and services

work.name: 8th color
work.summary: PullReview.com, automated code reviews for Ruby developers: first and only employee of the startup, 94% coverage, continuous deployment.
highlights: Sprint and roadmap: split big features into smaller releases, bundled security, upgrades and technical debt into sprints
Main developer: GitHub / BitBucket / GitLab integration (oauth login, REST API, git, push, pull requests), Stripe payments, notifications (email, HipChat, Slack)
Background analysis with Resque workers; integration and maintenance of quality tools (rubocop, brakeman, eslint, jscpd, simplecov)
Performance profiling and troubleshooting; upgrades (gems, rails, postgresql, passenger, debian)
Continuous deployment: feature branch, master, staging, one-click production deploy (capistrano, jenkins, errbit, god, batsd)
Puppetization of the infrastructure, tested with vagrant, rspec, puppet-lint, serverspec
Customer support, coaching of our intern

Consultancy (Aug - Oct 2014): yellow pages website (migration of 2 legacy MySQL databases to 1 PostgreSQL, facebook connect, geolocalized search), web scraping app for a price comparator (sidekiq), performance audit before launch (gatling, rack-mini-profiler)

work.name: M-Team
work.summary: Java technical architect, lead developer and coach on the insurance applications of M-Team (eclipse-rcp, spring, hibernate, ehcache, jquery, selenium, jenkins, sonar).
highlights: DPZ, digital platform for zorgverzekering (2012, 5 developers, 93% rules compliance, 90% coverage): build forge (jenkins, sonar), openpojo and selenium webdriver, technical coaching, technical debt management on a Vaadin app

Foa reengineering (2010-2011, 10 developers, 96% rules compliance, 80% coverage): migration path and bridging strategies (configuration, authentication, id generation), mockito / selenium2 / sonar integration-test coverage, promoted reuse of enterprise services

jadeR (2006-2010, 45 developers): industrialised Java development (nexus, hudson/jenkins, sonar, m2eclipse), custom sonar rules for SWT/Eclipse, an RCP bug reporter collecting evidence that saved time daily, a groovy console for live diagnostics and quick fixes on the cluster, nagios/jenkins monitoring, upgrades (spring 1.2 to 3.0, iSeries V6R1, jboss-cache to ehcache)

Carenet 24/7 (2010-2011): Mule, Spring, Jetty, DB2 based service providing insurability information 24/7 to care providers and pharmacists; webservices, SAML, certificates; high availability with failover from iSeries to DB2 linux; a DSL for message validation; designed for testability
Jade2 Accident & Security (2007-2008, 4 developers, 73,000 lines, 96% rules compliance, 75% coverage): accident suspicion detection, Workmen's Compensation Fund electronic flows

Jade2 (2006): assembled and tailored the default stack (spring, hibernate, ehcache, quartz, joda, eclipse rcp) for modularity, testability, portability and clustering, with built-in performance monitoring (AOP + JAMon) and AS/400 multi-tenant support
Jade1 (2003-2006): EJB 2 / Swing framework maintenance; migrations to a modular codebase, CVS, automated builds (ant, maven, java webstart), WebSphere 5

Deployment and production installation on client sites

projects.name: ORBF2 / Hesabu
projects.description: Performance-based financing: rule engine for RBF scheme calculations on top of DHIS2.
highlights: Implementation, configuration and customisation for country programs (Liberia, DRC, Cameroon, Ethiopia, ...)
orbf-rules_engine: rule engine for RBF scheme calculations (https://github.com/BLSQ/orbf-rules_engine)
go-hesabu: Go engine to solve the equations (https://github.com/BLSQ/go-hesabu)
hesabu-manager: DHIS2 app to manage Hesabu projects (https://github.com/BLSQ/hesabu-manager)

projects.name: Hosting and operations
projects.description: Hosting, monitoring and troubleshooting of DHIS2 and Bluesquare products, in the cloud and on premise.
highlights: DHIS2 hosting: around 50 instances, with a Slack bot for monitoring and troubleshooting

Diagnose report: one-shot HTML snapshot of a server for incident analysis (version, CPU / load, logs, running database queries, database sizes, thread stacks), extended from DHIS2 (Java) to Python apps (gunicorn thread dumps via faulthandler, where py-spy can't run)
Runbooks and practices: runbooks documenting recurring tasks, rules of engagement before touching a server, archiving of large tables (audit records) to keep databases manageable

Automated reviews: monthly AWS inventory snapshots and diffs, upgrade and deprecation checks (Elastic Beanstalk platforms, Docker images), access reviews (GitHub, Bitbucket, AWS users, outside collaborators), secret leak scanning (trufflehog), log review
Local hosting: on-premise deployment of Bluesquare products with docker and systemd (https://github.com/BLSQ/ops-local-hosting), with its toolbox (https://github.com/BLSQ/ops-local-hosting-toolbox)

projects.name: IASO
projects.description: Georegistry, data collection and microplanning platform.
highlights: DHIS2 integration: mapping of form questions to DHIS2 data elements for aggregate and event exports, org unit pyramid and groups sync, compatibility across DHIS2 versions (2.38 to 2.42), redesigned mapping screen (question tree, search, filters), import/export of mappings
Parquet exports via DuckDB: submissions and org unit pyramid (groups, parent ids), zstd compression; replaced the legacy CSV/XLSX submissions export

Scaling to larger org unit pyramids and more entities: N+1 query removal, indexes on large tables, faster mobile entity sync, faster exports (entities, users, submissions), org unit details, bulk imports with caching, faster test suite

Diagnostics tooling: explain_request command replaying a production API request with captured SQL, EXPLAIN plans and call stacks; QueryProfiler test helper breaking queries down by table and call site, estimating server time (RDS/S3 round trips), and locking query counts in tests to catch N+1 regressions

APM from access logs: DuckDB script parsing nginx and AWS load balancer logs, mapping paths to Django routes, reporting time per route and status, exported as Parquet for an HTML report running in the browser (DuckDB-WASM)

projects.name: Health campaign data (Ivory Coast)
projects.description: Data pipelines, dashboards and lightweight apps for health campaigns.
highlights: Health campaigns (CPS and MILDA, Ivory Coast): data pipelines and dashboards with OpenHEXA Python pipelines, Parquet, DuckDB and Superset

Promoted a "pre-baked app" pattern: OpenHEXA pipelines precompute the data as Parquet and PMTiles, served to lightweight apps (IASO apps, OpenHEXA web apps) that do most of the work in the browser, keeping the backend minimal
